overview: Poland is a country in Central Europe, on the Baltic Sea. Its capital and largest city is Warsaw. In the late 1700s Poland disappeared from the map when its neighbours divided it between them, and it became independent again in 1918. After decades of communist rule it became a democracy in 1989, and it joined NATO in 1999 and the European Union in 2004.

geography.text: Most of Poland is part of the North European Plain: low and flat, with farmland and forests. The Vistula, its longest river, flows north through Kraków and Warsaw to the Baltic Sea. The Masurian Lake District in the north-east has thousands of lakes, and the south rises into the Sudetes and the Carpathians, including the Tatra Mountains.

history.text: Poland became a Christian kingdom in 966 and, joined with Lithuania, was one of the largest states in Europe. It was divided up by Russia, Prussia and Austria and disappeared from the map in 1795. Reborn in 1918, Poland was invaded by Germany in 1939, starting the Second World War. The Solidarity movement helped bring down communism in 1989.

events.title: Union of Lublin
events.text: Poland and Lithuania form a commonwealth.

events.title: Wiped off the map
events.text: Poland is divided between Russia, Prussia and Austria.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Poland becomes an independent state again.

events.title: Invasion
events.text: Germany invades, starting the Second World War; the Soviet Union invades from the east.

events.title: End of communism
events.text: Solidarity wins elections and communist rule ends.

government.text: Poland is a parliamentary republic. Its parliament has two houses, the Sejm and the Senate. The Prime Minister leads the government, while the President, elected directly every five years, can veto laws. Poland joined NATO in 1999 and the European Union in 2004.

economy.text: Poland was the only EU economy that did not shrink during the 2008–09 financial crisis, and it has grown faster than most of Europe since 1990. It is strong in manufacturing, food, furniture and IT, and the video game company behind The Witcher is Polish. Poland uses its own currency, the złoty.

culture.text: Poland gave the world the composer Frédéric Chopin, the scientist Marie Curie, the astronomer Copernicus and Pope John Paul II. Its cities were rebuilt after the destruction of the Second World War; Warsaw's Old Town was reconstructed so carefully that UNESCO lists it.

items.title: Marie Curie
items.text: Born in Warsaw; the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences.

items.title: Copernicus
items.text: Argued in 1543 that the Earth moves around the Sun.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Robert Lewandowski is one of the greatest strikers of his generation. Volleyball and ski jumping draw huge audiences, and Iga Świątek became tennis world number one.

items.title: Robert Lewandowski
items.text: Scored five goals in nine minutes for Bayern Munich in 2015.

items.title: Iga Świątek
items.text: Won the French Open four times.
